sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.
Heard the learned counsel for revision petitioner and also the counsel appearing for the respondent-State.
2. This revision petition is filed challenging the allowing the application filed under Section 239 of Cr.P.C to discharge the accuse for all the offences.
This revision petitioner is arrayed as accused No.3.
The Trial Court allowed the application in part in respect of all the accused Nos.1 to 5 for offences punishable under Section 417 and 420 of I.P.C.
The accused No.5 has also discharged for the offence punishable under Section 504 R/w Section 34 of I.P.C and also Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

The main contention of the counsel appearing for the revision petitioner in this revision petition that the Trial Court committed an error in not discharging this revision petitioner and this revision petitioner is a married sister and only an omnibus allegation is made against the petitioner and not disputed the facts of engagement and also the marriage date is fixed and also having given the advance for the marriage.
The counsel only contend that this revision petitioner has been falsely implicated in this case and she has not played any role.
Only with an intention to falsely implicate her in the complaint as well as in statement of witnesses, the same has been referred.
Hence, this Court can exercise the revisional powers.
4. Per Contra, the counsel appearing for the respondent-State would submits that specific allegation is made in the complaint as well as in the statement of witnesses.

Now, the statements which have been produced before the Court also clearly discloses for having made the further statement of complaint as well as the witnesses Shivarangaiah, Puttaraju, N.Shivanandan and NC:
2024:KHC:10241 Krishnappa, all of them have referred the role played by this Court in engaging her Sushma K vs State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129688026/
2 marriage and also the demand made by all the family members and also when the complainant and their family members could not able to meet their demand, the marriage was cancelled.

sentences.text:
Thereafter,
complaint was given along with all documents for having made the arrangements of the marriage,
the same has taken note of by the Trial Court.

5. Having heard the revision petitioner's counsel and also the counsel appearing for the respondent -State and also looking into the averments made in the complaint, specific allegation is also made against this petitioner that all of them have made the demand to pay an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- as cash and also 600 grams of gold and witnesses who have made the statement before the I.O also re-iterated the averments of complaint in their statement and apart from that specific allegation is also made that when the complaint was given this petitioner also went to Police Station but did not bring the bride groom and also the specific allegation is made in the NC: 2024:KHC:10241 statement also that when all of them went to the house of the witnesses and made demand.

When such specific allegations are made with regard to role played by this revision petitioner and the very contention of the revision petitioner that only omnibus allegation is made against this revision petitioner and she is married sister of bride groom cannot be accepted.
The Trial Court having taken note of material available on record, rightly allowed the application in part for the offences, when the Court found no ingredients of certain offences.
Hence, I do not find any error committed by the Trial Court in allowing the application in part.

The Trial Court also in paragraph No.11 discussed the allegations made in the compliant and also participation of accused No.3 also along with other accused Nos.1 to 4 and also taken note of the principles laid down in the judgment which are referred in paragraph No.12.

Having considered the material available on record, reasoned order has been passed and rightly comes to the conclusion that it requires full fledged trial and charges leveled against accused Nos.1 to 4 considering the NC: 2024:KHC:10241 statement of witnesses and allegation made in the complaint.
Hence, I do not find any merit to interfere with the order of the Trial Court.

6. In view of the discussions made above, I pass the following:
ORDER The Criminal Revision Petition is dismissed.
